## Collected data and analysis for session `933a1ab3-1630-48a3-b35a-3087d7b2603c` (links-notation#315 → PR #319) ### Logs and sources | What | Where | |---|---| | Full start-command log of the container (75,126 lines, 4.9 MB), uploaded with `$ --upload-log 933a1ab3-1630-48a3-b35a-3087d7b2603c` (private gist) | https://gist.github.com/konard/22cf5410b21feb9e12c76e6e9582ad10 | | Failure log attached by solve | https://gist.githubusercontent.com/konard/57e1927f923c6593a70e15bf7733a7a9/raw/5f49125a115015754e180fedabc5032c23feddb1/tmp-hive-mind-log-upload-MzdBtR-sanitized.log.txt | | Intermediate ("killed session") log | https://gist.githubusercontent.com/konard/d495a372e5466f9396ca8aa44ad2c722/raw/2b7cd268040268f06c85daa82ea22158ec35f661/tmp-hive-mind-log-upload-GimKvv-sanitized.log.txt | | PR comments | [failure](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/pull/319#issuecomment-5837901286), [intermediate log](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/pull/319#issuecomment-5837915561), [OOM "recovered" notice](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/pull/319#issuecomment-5837915932) | | Container | `12b7df9bfed0` still exists (`Exited (1)`, kept because `OOMKilled=true`); **not** removed, so it's available for inspection | | Claude session | `85671f31-4459-422e-8fef-04ee03fd3aa0`, transcript on the host under `~/.claude/projects/-tmp-gh-issue-solver-1790359116497/` | | Bot log / state | `~/.hive-mind/logs/telegram-bot.log`, `~/.hive-mind/state/sessions-events.jsonl` (excerpts below) |
$ --status 933a1ab3-1630-48a3-b35a-3087d7b2603c ``` 78e04f1d-c4b3-4ba1-90eb-96091f22dd62 status executed exitCode 1 logPath /tmp/start-command/logs/isolation/docker/78e04f1d-c4b3-4ba1-90eb-96091f22dd62.log startTime "2026-09-25T17:57:47.900Z" endTime "2026-09-25T18:54:16.585Z" endTimeSource docker-finished-at oomKilled true exitReason "memory-exhaustion (cgroup-oom-killer)" memoryExhausted true memoryExhaustedReason "Docker reported State.OOMKilled=true" options isolated docker, isolationMode detached image "konard/hive-mind-dind:2.32.0" volumes ".../.claude/.credentials.json:... (single-file mount, see #2296), .../.claude/projects, .../.claude/sessions, .config/gh, .gitconfig" keepContainer false, keepContainerOnFail false ``` Command: `solve https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/issues/315 --think high --auto-merge --tool claude --attach-logs --verbose --no-tool-check --disable-report-issue --language en` (solve v2.32.0, Claude Code with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, `permissionMode: bypassPermissions`).
### Timeline (UTC, 2026-09-25) | Time | Event | Source | |---|---|---| | 17:57:49 | Container started; Claude session `85671f31…` started in `/tmp/gh-issue-solver-1790359116497` | start-command log | | ~18:0x–18:40 | The agent runs stack-overflow probes in several languages (Rust, Go, C#, Java, PHP, Python), and starts parallel "port" subagents plus background commands (**11** `run_in_background` tool calls) | log | | 18:12:47 | Host: **0.6 GB available of 11.7 GB**, load 12.4, 3 active sessions | bot heartbeat | | ~18:13 | The kernel OOM-kills **child experiment processes**: the Go probe (`parens 50000: … signal: killed`; deep recursion grows the goroutine stack towards the 1 GB default limit) and `dotnet …/Probe.dll` (`line 77: 69856 Killed`). Docker sets `State.OOMKilled=true` for the container. **The solve and Claude processes are not killed and keep working for ~40 more minutes.** | log lines 54953, 59958 | | 18:13:10 | hive-mind records "Detected at" for an OOM kill | PR notice | | ~18:53 | The agent's last message: *"The experiments README is committed. The rest (version bump, test comparison, PR description) depends on the port agents, so I'm waiting for them to finish."* It then **ends its turn**: result `subtype: success`, `terminal_reason: completed`, `permission_denials: []`, cost $12.19 | log lines 74637–74778 | | 18:53:5x | Because this is `claude -p` stream mode, ending the turn ends the process. Claude Code stops the still-running background tasks (`task_notification status: stopped`: `go test -race …`, the C# probe, the port subagents). Their pending tool calls come back as **synthetic** `tool_result` = `"User rejected tool use"` / "The user doesn't want to proceed with this tool use… STOP…", and the subagents' transcripts end with `[Request interrupted by user]` | log lines 74792–74925 | | 18:53:5x | solve: `⚠️ Tool result error detected …` ×3 → `❌ Command failed: Final tool result failed: The user doesn't want to proceed…` → classified as **CLAUDE execution failed** | log line 74935 | | 18:53:54 | solve auto-commits (`🛟 Auto-commit before critical-error recovery`, `e4dd097`, 26 files, +2415/−235) and pushes it. **No work lost.** PR #319 stays **draft** | log, PR | | 18:54:13 | PR comment "🚨 Solution Draft Failed" | PR | | 18:54:16 | Container exits with code 1; kept because `OOMKilled=true` | `$ --status` | | 18:55:05–06 | PR comments: intermediate log, and "⚠️ Working session recovered from out of memory … 🔄 **A new working session was started** to recover from this event" (`--on-session-kill=resume`) | PR | | 18:55:07 | Bot: `session_completion_notified {"exitCode":1,"status":"failed"}` → `Removed session … from snapshot` → `session_completed`. **No new session was ever started.** No start-command session for links-notation#315/PR #319 exists after 18:54 | bot log, `sessions-events.jsonl`, `/tmp/start-command/logs` | ### Root causes **1. The "The user doesn't want to proceed with this tool use" failure is a false positive. It is not a permission check or classifier.** - Claude Code ran with `bypassPermissions`, and the final result reports `permission_denials: []`, `subtype: success`, `terminal_reason: completed`. No permission or tool classifier ran. - The texts `User rejected tool use` / `The user doesn't want to proceed…` / `[Request interrupted by user]` are what Claude Code writes for tool calls that are **cancelled**. Here they were the background tasks and subagents it stopped when the print-mode process exited after the result event. - solve's "final tool result" check scans events **after** the result event and treats those synthetic cancellations as a tool failure. **Fixes:** - Treat the `result` event as authoritative, and ignore `tool_result`s with `is_error`/"User rejected tool use" that arrive after it. - In particular, ignore those with a `parent_tool_use_id` (subagent/background) or paired with `task_notification status: stopped`. - Record them as "background tasks cancelled at exit: N" instead. **2. The real problem: the agent ended its turn to "wait for" background agents, which print mode doesn't support.** - In `claude -p` (single prompt, stream-json output) nothing re-invokes the model after `end_turn`. So "I'm waiting for them to finish" is fatal: the process exits and the background work (port subagents, `go test -race`, probes) is killed half-way. The remaining steps (version bump, test comparison, PR description) were never done. **Fixes (pick one or combine):** - **(a)** In autonomous mode, tell the model in the system prompt that it must not end its turn while background tasks or subagents are running, and must wait for them (poll/`TaskOutput`/foreground) before finishing. Or disable `run_in_background` for Agent/Bash in non-interactive runs. - **(b)** Detect this case: the result text says it is waiting, or `task_notification`s are stopped after the result, or subagent transcripts end with `[Request interrupted by user]`. Then **auto-resume** the same session (`claude --resume 85671f31… -p "Continue: background tasks were cancelled when the previous turn ended; re-run them in the foreground and finish the remaining steps."`) at least once. - **(c)** Use stream-json **input** mode and keep stdin open, so the CLI keeps running and the model is re-invoked when background tasks finish. **3. The "recovered from out of memory" notice is wrong on two counts.** - **Wrong diagnosis:** Docker's `State.OOMKilled` is set when *any* process in the container cgroup is OOM-killed. Here it was the agent's own experiment children (Go/.NET deep-recursion probes). The session itself was never killed. It ran for 40 more minutes and ended normally. The notice then quotes "9.8 GB of 11.7 GB RAM available" as its "out of memory" evidence, which contradicts itself. - **False promise:** it says "🔄 A new working session was started", but the bot log shows the session was completed as `failed` and removed at 18:55:07 with no new session. `--on-session-kill=resume` didn't resume anything. **Fixes:** - Distinguish "session process OOM-killed" (solve/claude PID gone, abnormal exit) from "a child process was OOM-killed" (container flag only). For the latter, don't treat the session as killed; just report it (which process, when) as a warning. - Post "a new working session was started" only **after** the new session has actually been started, with its session ID and a link. Otherwise say it failed and why. - Make sure the resume path runs for exit-code-1 + OOMKilled containers too. Currently the completion handler treats the run as "failed" and never reaches `on-session-kill=resume`. **4. Memory safety for experiments.** - Three concurrent sessions on a 6-CPU/11.7 GB host plus unbounded-recursion probes brought the host down to 0.6 GB available. - **Fixes:** per-task cgroup memory limits (`docker run --memory`, maybe `--memory-swap`), so one task's probes can't starve the others. Also tell agents in the system prompt to bound experiments that deliberately exhaust stack or memory (`ulimit -v`, `GOMEMLIMIT`, `debug.SetMaxStack`, `timeout`). The Go probe at depth 50000 took 37.8 s and was then OOM-killed. **5. About "codex attempting to use a tool classifier":** this session used `--tool claude`, not codex, and the rejection texts come from Claude Code's cancellation of background tasks (point 1), not from a tool classifier or a user-feedback request. If there is a separate codex session showing a classifier or approval prompt, its session ID/log is needed. For codex, non-interactive runs should use `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` (or `approval_policy = "never"`), so that no approval or feedback step can ever be requested. ### Related - #2296: the same host and day; single-file credential mounts are also used by this session. - #2293: false-positive and false-negative classification in solve's restart/failure logic (same class as point 1 and point 3). - #2134: the kill-notice/resume mechanism quoted in the notice.
